comments.body:
Root cause. `PostgresIntakeRetryStore.clear_intake_dedup` interpolated the repository name into a SQL LIKE pattern via `side_effects.c.target.like(f"%:{repo}")`. In LIKE, `_` matches any single character, and GitHub repository names may contain underscores.

Investigation followed the debugging protocol. The over-match was confirmed against the running database rather than inferred. `select 'ADEV-1:myXrepo' like '%:my_repo'` returns true.

Direction of the defect. Over-deletion only. GitHub repository names admit `_` but not `%`, and `_` widens a pattern rather than narrowing it, so the clear can never delete too few rows. It can delete a row belonging to a different repository that shares the ticket key, which makes that ticket re-admittable.

Why this matters now. ADEVX-140 made a finished run reach `COMPLETED` immediately, removing the accidental re-admission block a lingering `PR_CREATED` execution row used to provide. ADEVX-141 made this ledger row the deliberate guard. An unintended clear therefore produces a duplicate run rather than being absorbed.

Why the suite missed it. `PostgresIntakeRetryStore` had no unit coverage at all. The existing tests substitute a `_FakeStore` at the protocol boundary, which bypasses the SQL. This change adds the first coverage of that class.

Fix. Candidate rows are selected by task id and operation, filtered on the parsed repository suffix literally in Python, then deleted by exact `side_effect_key`. The no-repository path still clears every `intake_start` row for the ticket in a single delete. The parser `intake_start_target_repo` that ADEVX-141 introduced in `services/coordination/idempotency.py` was made public so both call sites share one implementation rather than keeping two that can drift.

Falsification. The ledger test double implements SQL LIKE semantics faithfully by translating `%` and `_` to their LIKE meanings, so the regression test is behavioural rather than a structural assertion about the SQL text. Reverting the production body to the LIKE form fails `clearing_intake_dedup_treats_underscores_in_the_repo_literally` with `assert 2 == 1`, which is the over-delete itself. An earlier revert attempt appeared to pass because the patch matched the Protocol stub rather than the implementation. That was caught and redone against the implementation body.

Impact analysis. `clear_intake_dedup` has one production caller at `intake_retry.py:97`, reached through a Protocol. Only the Postgres implementation body changed, so the two existing test fakes are unaffected. `intake_start_target_repo` had three references, all inside `idempotency.py`. Risk LOW.

Gates. `inv ci` at `1289c50`: 1478 passed, 6 skipped, eval-gate PASS, exit 0. All 5 selectors proven individually. Plan review PASS. Code review PASS at `1289c50`, 0 blocking, 0 advisory. The first plan review flagged one criterion bundling two deliverables with "and", so that criterion and its test were split into per-ticket removal and cross-ticket isolation cases.

compiled_state.description:
`PostgresIntakeRetryStore.clear_intake_dedup` scoped its delete with `side_effects.c.target.like(f"%:{repo}")` at `services/orchestration/intake_retry.py:125`. The repository name is interpolated into a SQL LIKE pattern, where `_` matches any single character and `%` matches any run of characters. GitHub repository names may contain underscores, so a clear for `my_repo` also matches a target belonging to `myXrepo`.

Confirmed against the running database. `select 'ADEV-1:myXrepo' like '%:my_repo'` returns true.

The consequence is over-deletion on the operator clear path. `inv intake --retry` for one repository removes the `intake_start` ledger row belonging to a different repository that shares the ticket key, which makes that other ticket re-admittable. ADEVX-141 made this ledger row the only guard against a duplicate intake run, so an unintended clear now produces a duplicate run rather than being absorbed by a lingering execution row.

`PostgresIntakeRetryStore` had no unit coverage. The existing tests substitute a `_FakeStore` at the protocol boundary, which bypasses the SQL entirely, so the defect was invisible to the suite.

The fix applies the repository scope literally rather than as a pattern, reusing the parse helper ADEVX-141 introduced for the same rule in `services/coordination/idempotency.py`. Candidate rows are selected by task id and operation, filtered on the parsed repository suffix in Python, then deleted by exact `side_effect_key`. The no-repository path still clears every `intake_start` row for the ticket.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Clearing intake dedup for a repository whose name contains an underscore leaves another repository's row intact, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_intake_retry.py -k clearing_intake_dedup_treats_underscores_in_the_repo_literally`
- [x] Clearing intake dedup without a repository removes every intake row for the ticket, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_intake_retry.py -k clearing_intake_dedup_without_a_repo_clears_every_intake_row`
- [x] Clearing intake dedup without a repository leaves other tickets' intake rows intact, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_intake_retry.py -k clearing_intake_dedup_without_a_repo_spares_other_tickets`
- [x] Clearing intake dedup for a repository with no matching row deletes nothing, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_intake_retry.py -k clearing_intake_dedup_for_an_unmatched_repo_deletes_nothing`
- [x] The repository suffix parser remains shared with the idempotency ledger, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_coordination_idempotency.py -k legacy_intake_repo_match_treats_underscores_literally`

## Testing
Run each acceptance criterion selector on its own. Run `PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/inv ci` before closing the ticket.
